title: Flaky windows test: matching-host Ladybug launcher version assertion fails on an identical tree
description:
FLAKE CONFIRMED BY TREE IDENTITY, not by judgement. test/ladybug-package-qualification.test.ts:84, "matching-host Ladybug package qualification > the published launcher reports the real compiled Lore version through synchronous redirected output", in lint/typecheck/test (windows-latest).

THREE MEASUREMENTS, THE SAME BYTES, BOTH OUTCOMES:

  #207 head  82bbf578  tree 46925743e10843d4b0b8d51bb9d05f041b3b9cc0  windows PASSED
  push/main  1f34f8a3  tree 46925743e10843d4b0b8d51bb9d05f041b3b9cc0  windows FAILED  (run 35545097732, attempt 1)
  push/main  1f34f8a3  tree 46925743e10843d4b0b8d51bb9d05f041b3b9cc0  windows PASSED  (run 35545097732, attempt 2)

Byte-identical trees roughly three minutes apart, then the SAME SHA passing on re-run with nothing changed. The promoted set was five .quest/tasks/*.json files and nothing else; the failing assertion concerns a compiled launcher reporting its version, which no tracker JSON can reach. Attempt 1 reported 3195 pass / 141 skip / 1 fail across 3337 tests in 105 files.

WHY IT MATTERS RATHER THAN BEING NOISE. This job is one of the five required contexts on dev (require-ci-on-dev, ruleset 22838594), so a flake here blocks a merge into dev; and it reddened main's post-promotion push run, which is the run that carries the `main is fast-forward of dev` guard. The guard itself passed. But a reader who takes the run's CONCLUSION rather than its job list sees a failed promotion, which is exactly the two-reds-one-colour trap this repository's profile already warns about -- here arriving as one red BY DESIGN on the pull_request run and one red BY ACCIDENT on the push run, on the same SHA.

WHAT THE FAILURE PROBABLY IS, EXPLICITLY UNVERIFIED. The failing test was reported at [2056.37ms]. The test compiles a real Windows binary at line 103 via packageCompileCommand with timeout: 120_000, then asserts expect(compile.exitCode).toBe(0) at line 109 before spawning the launcher. Two seconds is far too fast for a bun --compile to have run, so the likely shape is a FAST compile failure surfacing at line 109 rather than a timeout or an output race -- a transient temp-dir, antivirus, or file-lock condition on the windows runner would fit. THIS IS A HYPOTHESIS, not a reading of the error.

EVIDENCE LOST, AND HOW: I re-ran the failed job before extracting the assertion text, and GitHub REPLACES a job's log on re-run for the same job id. Attempt 1's expect() output is unrecoverable; only the summary lines captured beforehand survive. The operational rule this earns: CAPTURE THE FAILING LOG BEFORE RE-RUNNING, because the re-run is what destroys the thing that would diagnose it. Next occurrence should run `gh run view --job <id> --log-failed > <file>` first, and only then re-run.

Note the repo already carries flake machinery for a different windows condition: the test step retries on "error: EEXIST: file already exists, epoll_ctl" or exit 124, with --max-concurrency and --timeout reduced on the retry. Whatever this is, it is not that one -- it is not caught by that grep.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The failure mode is identified from a CAPTURED failing log, not inferred -- the next occurrence is logged to a file before any re-run
Whether the failure is the line-109 compile assertion or the launcher spawn is settled with evidence, closing the hypothesis in this record rather than restating it
The test is made deterministic, or its transient condition is detected and retried the way the existing epoll_ctl/exit-124 retry already handles its own case -- not simply re-run by hand
A flake in this job is distinguishable from a real failure without tree-diffing by hand, since it is a required context on dev and can redden a promotion push run

implementationNotes:
FAILURE MODE IDENTIFIED FROM THE CAPTURED LOG, AND THE HYPOTHESIS IN THIS RECORD IS REFUTED. It is not the line-109 compile assertion and not the launcher spawn. Every assertion in the try block PASSED; the cleanup threw:

  test/ladybug-package-qualification.test.ts:
    120 |       } finally {
    121 |         rmSync(root, { recursive: true, force: true });
                  ^
  error: EBUSY: resource busy or locked, rm 'C:\Users\RUNNER~1\AppData\Local\Temp\lore-windows-launcher-test-0FwZ5G'
    at .../test/ladybug-package-qualification.test.ts:121:9

Windows retains a handle on the scratch tree briefly after the compiled launcher process exits, so the REMOVE is what races. That also explains the [2056.37ms] this record found suspicious: the time is real work completing successfully, not a compile that never ran.

THE EVIDENCE WAS NOT LOST, AND THE OPERATIONAL RULE THIS RECORD DERIVED IS WRONG IN ITS MECHANISM. This record states that "GitHub REPLACES a job's log on re-run for the same job id" and that attempt 1's expect() output is unrecoverable. A re-run creates a NEW JOB ID PER ATTEMPT, and the old attempt's job keeps serving its own log indefinitely. Measured on this very run, 35545097732: attempt 1's windows job is 106169476606 (failure), attempt 2's is 106170112304 (success). Fetching 106169476606's log four hours and one green re-run later returned 642362 bytes containing the full assertion text quoted above.

  gh api "repos/opum-ai/lore-cli/actions/runs/<run_id>/attempts/1/jobs" \
    -q '.jobs[] | "\(.id) \(.name) \(.conclusion)"'
  gh api "repos/opum-ai/lore-cli/actions/jobs/<that_id>/logs" \
    --allow-escape-sequences > failing.log

--allow-escape-sequences is NOT optional and is why this looked unrecoverable: without it gh writes ZERO BYTES and exits 1 with a message about terminal escape sequences, which reads exactly like the log being gone. The first attempt here produced exit=1 bytes=0 and would have confirmed the "evidence lost" conclusion to anyone who stopped there.

WHAT IS GENUINELY REPLACED ON A RE-RUN IS RUN ARTIFACTS, not job logs, and this repository had already measured that -- docs/reference/lore-cli-release-truth.md's LCLI-531 addendum records artifacts being silently replaced with no /attempts/1/artifacts endpoint to recover them. Generalising that correct finding about artifacts to logs is what produced the wrong rule here. Two different objects, one re-run.

THE FIX USES MACHINERY THIS FILE ALREADY HAD. removeQualificationScratch (benchmark/ladybug/package-qualification.ts:1011) is a bounded linear-backoff remover -- 11 attempts, 250ms * (n+1) -- whose isRetryableRemovalError already lists EBUSY, and which calls makeTreeWritable first. The file unit-tests it directly (the "retries temporary Windows-style scratch locks with bounded linear backoff" test, which PASSED in the same run four lines below the failure). The failing test was simply not using it. This is AC[2]'s "detected and retried the way the existing retry already handles its own case", satisfied by routing to the existing retry rather than inventing a second one.

One constraint the fix had to respect: removeQualificationScratch REFUSES any path outside the "lore-ladybug-package-" prefix convention, which is the guard that makes it safe to hand a recursive delete a runtime-computed path. The launcher test's scratch was "lore-windows-launcher-test-", so the prefix moved to "lore-ladybug-package-windows-launcher-" rather than the guard being relaxed.

PROVEN BY MUTATION, NOT ONLY BY PASSING. The new test asserts both halves of that contract -- the prefix in use is accepted, and a prefix outside the convention is refused and leaves the directory intact. Relaxing the guard in package-qualification.ts reddens EXACTLY 1 of 15 tests, the new one, while the existing backoff test stays green because the mutant genuinely preserves what that test asserts. A mutation that reddened everything would not have localised anything.

SECOND HOST CHECKED, not assumed: the other bare rmSync in this file (the isolated-store test) only writes plain JSON files and never spawns a process or compiles a binary, so nothing holds a handle on its tree. Left alone -- changing it would be scope creep with no evidence behind it.

CANNOT BE EXERCISED ON THIS WORKSTATION. The launcher test is matching-host and skips on macOS (14 pass, 1 skip locally). The EBUSY path itself is covered by the existing unit test, which injects the error rather than needing Windows. The real proof is the windows-latest job on this PR.
finalSummary:
Fixed the windows Ladybug launcher flake, delivered in opum-ai/lore-cli#220 (CI run 35561150958, the PR head's own run). The recorded hypothesis was wrong and the evidence this record declared unrecoverable was recovered.

THE FAILURE IS THE CLEANUP, NOT THE COMPILE. Every assertion in the try block passed; rmSync at test/ladybug-package-qualification.test.ts:121 threw "EBUSY: resource busy or locked" on the scratch tree, because Windows retains a handle briefly after the compiled launcher process exits. The [2056.37ms] this record flagged as too fast for a bun --compile is real work completing successfully, not a compile that never ran.

THE LOG SURVIVES A RE-RUN, which refutes this record's derived operational rule. A re-run creates a NEW JOB ID PER ATTEMPT, so the old attempt keeps serving its own log indefinitely: on run 35545097732, attempt 1's windows job is 106169476606 (failure) and attempt 2's is 106170112304 (success), and fetching 106169476606's log four hours and one green re-run later returned 642362 bytes with the full assertion text. What a re-run genuinely replaces is run ARTIFACTS, which this repository had already measured in docs/reference/lore-cli-release-truth.md's LCLI-531 addendum. Generalising that correct artifact finding to logs is what produced the wrong rule. --allow-escape-sequences is why it looked unrecoverable: without it gh writes ZERO BYTES and exits 1, which reads exactly like the log being gone, and the first attempt here did exactly that.

THE FIX ROUTES TO MACHINERY THE FILE ALREADY HAD rather than inventing a second retry. removeQualificationScratch (package-qualification.ts:1011) is a bounded linear-backoff remover, 11 attempts at 250ms*(n+1), with EBUSY already in isRetryableRemovalError and makeTreeWritable called first. The same file unit-tests it FOUR LINES BELOW the failure, and that test passed in the same failing run. Its prefix guard refuses paths outside "lore-ladybug-package-", which is what makes handing it a runtime-computed recursive delete safe, so the launcher scratch prefix moved instead of the guard being relaxed.

PROVEN BY MUTATION. A new test asserts both halves of the prefix contract: the prefix in use is accepted, and one outside the convention is refused AND leaves the directory intact. Relaxing the guard reddens exactly 1 of 15 tests -- the new one -- while the existing backoff test stays green because the mutant genuinely preserves what it asserts. The mutated file was restored and verified by diff against HEAD rather than by re-reading a subject line.

ci.yml's flake-triage block gains the recovery method, the --allow-escape-sequences trap, and why it matters: tree identity proves a flake WITHOUT saying what broke, and both of that block's triage questions need to know what broke. Comment-only -- no logic, no job names, no if:/paths changes -- so the required-context surface is untouched and the file still parses.

Second host checked rather than assumed: the other bare rmSync in this file only writes plain JSON and never spawns a process, so nothing holds a handle on its tree. Left alone.

LIMIT ON THE PROOF, stated because it is the one thing this workstation cannot close: the EBUSY path cannot be exercised on macOS, where the launcher test is matching-host and skips (14 pass, 1 skip, 0 fail locally). The injected-error unit test covers the retry logic without needing Windows, but the real proof is the lint/typecheck/test (windows-latest) job on this PR. Gates otherwise: typecheck clean, lint shows the same 3 pre-existing warnings as dev (confirmed by stashing) none in the touched files, bun run lore check exits 0.
